MVTec and BMG bring HALCON procedures to ctrlX OS

Nexeed Integrated Vision connects machine-vision procedures with Bosch Rexroth’s control environment for inspection and robot guidance.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗5 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

Vision joins the control environment

MVTec, Bosch Manufacturing Solutions (BMG) and Bosch Rexroth announced their collaboration on November 5. MVTec and BMG join ctrlX World, aiming to simplify how machine builders and integrators combine vision with other automation functions.

How the components fit

HALCON supplies image-processing procedures, while BMG’s Nexeed Integrated Vision app makes them available on ctrlX OS. The Linux-based environment underpins ctrlX CORE and is also hardware-independent, providing a defined link between vision and control technology.

Applications and validation

Potential uses include inspection, identification, measurement and robot guidance, using rule-based vision, 3D methods or deep learning. The partners claim reduced integration work but provide no universal time-saving benchmark. Camera, lighting and machine-cycle requirements still need application-specific validation.
